tools.name: server_info
tools.description: Get the CouchDB server welcome document: version, git sha, instance uuid, enabled features and vendor

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Get the CouchDB session for the configured credentials: the authenticated user name, its roles and the handlers the server offers

tools.name: list_databases
tools.description: List the database names on the CouchDB server

limit.description: Max database names to return (default 20, max 100)

skip.description: Optional number of database names to skip before returning results

tools.name: get_database
tools.description: Get one CouchDB database's document counts, update sequence, on-disk sizes and cluster parameters

db.description: Database name as returned by list_databases

tools.name: list_docs
tools.description: List document ids and revisions in one CouchDB database, without fetching document bodies

db.description: Database name as returned by list_databases

skip.description: Optional number of documents to skip before returning results

descending.description: Return the ids in descending key order

tools.name: get_changes
tools.description: Get the recent changes feed for one CouchDB database: changed document ids, their sequences and the current last sequence

db.description: Database name as returned by list_databases

needs_review: CouchDB is customer-hosted, so base_url comes from the credential and nothing here is provable against a vendor-run endpoint. Every tool is GET-only and the spec stays unproven until the live harness runs it against a real ephemeral container

GET /_all_dbs requires a server admin in CouchDB 3.x, so list_databases answers 401 for a database-scoped user even though whoami and get_database succeed for that same user. Documented, not fixable in the spec

list_databases returns a top-level array of STRINGS, which response.pick cannot address (a root-array pick maps sub-picks over objects). It therefore ships with truncate only and no pick, so the whole array reaches the caller
get_changes uses the default feed=normal. The continuous and longpoll feeds stream and would hold the 15s runtime request open, so they are deliberately not exposed
_changes and _all_docs both answer 200 on an empty database (empty results plus a last_seq or total_rows 0), which is the expected fresh-instance result
Single-document reads (GET /{db}/{docid}) are not wired: a fresh instance is not guaranteed to hold any document, so the tool could not carry a resolvable _probe
The _probe database name is quoxproof-live, which the live provisioner creates. On a server without it, get_database, list_docs and get_changes answer 404
